newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak stocks mixed in dull trading, SAX up 0.49.
newsitem.headline: Slovak stocks mixed in dull trading, SAX up 0.49.

text.p: Slovak shares were mixed in dull trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with the official SAX index closing up 0.49 points at 166.71.
Some blue chips closed firmer, but brokers said it was too early to celebrate as volumes were too small to indicate a trend.
"The volumes of traded shares are still desperately low, urging us to remain cautious," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
Steel maker VSZ closed up one crown at 630, on a volume of 370 shares. Oil refiner Slovnaft increased by 21 crowns to 830, on 12 shares traded, pushing the index up.
"I don't expect this to become a trend, though some prices begin to look quite good at the moment," Briska said.
"There is no rush to the market, which would boost trading at these attractive values (prices), at the beginning of summer," he added.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta lost 100 crowns, closing at 1,100 on volume of 10 shares, preventing the SAX from rising further.
Overall, volume fell to 373,492 shares from 823,583 shares traded on Friday, while turnover eased to 174.94 million crowns from 266.33 million.
Both the volume and turnover were boosted by direct trades.
